messages.content: Find out about traffic laws in Texas.

function.name: lawsuit_search
function.description: Search for lawsuits related to a particular subject matter in a certain location. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

location.description: The location to perform the search in.

subject.description: The subject matter of the lawsuits.

year.description: Optional. The year in which the lawsuit was filed. Default: 2024

message.content:
**Traffic Laws in Texas (as of 2024)** | Topic | Key Points | Notes | |-------|------------|-------| | **Speed Limits** | • Posted limits are the law.
• Exceeding by 5 mph or more is a misdemeanor.
• Exceeding by 10 mph or more is a felony. | Speed limits vary by road type (e.g., 55‑70 mph on highways, 25‑35 mph in residential areas). | | **Seat‑belt & Child‑seat** | • All occupants must wear seat belts.
• Children under 8 must be in a child safety seat or booster. | Failure to buckle up is a misdemeanor. | | **Driving Under Influence (DUI)** | • Blood alcohol concentration (BAC) ≥ 0.08% is illegal.
• Penalties include fines, license suspension, and possible jail time. | First offense: $1,000 fine, 30‑90 days license suspension. | | **Cell‑phone Use** | • Hand‑held phone use while driving is prohibited.
• Hands‑free devices are allowed. | Violations are misdemeanors; repeat offenders face higher penalties. | | **Right‑of‑Way** | • Stop at red lights and stop signs.
• Yield to pedestrians in crosswalks. | Failure to yield can result in fines and points on the license. | | **Parking Regulations** | • No parking in fire lanes, handicap spaces (unless you have a permit), or on sidewalks.
• Parking in a no‑parking zone is a misdemeanor. | Parking tickets are typically civil fines. | | **Traffic School** | • Eligible for first‑time offenders with a clean record.
• Completion can prevent points on the license. | Must be approved by the court. | | **Points System** | • Points are added for violations (e.g., 2 points for speeding 5‑10 mph over limit).
• Accumulating 12 points in 3 years leads to license suspension. | Points stay on record for 3 years. | | **Vehicle Registration & Inspection** | • Annual registration renewal required.
• Vehicles must pass an annual safety inspection. | Failure to register or inspect can lead to fines and impoundment. | | **Insurance Requirements** | • Minimum liability coverage: $30,000 for bodily injury per person, $60,000 for bodily injury per accident, $25,000 for property damage. | Driving without insurance is a felony. | | **School Bus Rules** | • Vehicles must stop when a school bus is loading/unloading children.
• Failure to stop is a misdemeanor. | Applies to all vehicles, including motorcycles. | | **Lane‑Changing & Overtaking** | • Must signal and check mirrors/blind spots.
• Overtaking on the right is prohibited unless the lane is marked for passing. | Violations can result in fines and points. | | **Emergency Vehicles** | • Must yield to emergency vehicles with flashing lights or sirens. | Failure to yield can lead to fines and points. | | **Towing & Impoundment** | • Vehicles parked illegally may be towed.
• Towed vehicles must be retrieved within 48 hours to avoid impound fees. | Towing fees are typically civil. | | **Special Permits** | • Commercial drivers need a CDL.
• Certain vehicles (e.g., farm equipment) may require special permits. | CDL violations are serious and can lead to license revocation. | **How to Stay Updated** 1. **Texas Department of Transportation (TxDOT)** – Official website for traffic regulations and updates. 2. **Texas Transportation Code** – The legal text governing all traffic laws. 3. **Local County Courts** – For specific local ordinances and court rulings. 4. **Texas Department of Motor Vehicles (TxDMV)** – For registration, insurance, and licensing information. **Quick Tips** - Always obey posted speed limits and traffic signals. - Keep your vehicle’s registration and inspection current. - Carry proof of insurance at all times. - Avoid using a handheld phone while driving. - If you’re unsure about a specific rule, consult TxDOT or a local attorney. Feel free to ask if you need details on a particular aspect of Texas traffic law!
